-- Workflow D: everything the form and the re-check need for ONE person, as one row.
-- matches = all of the person's matches on active products (LIKELY ones carry the product's
-- soft_rules so unverified rule texts can be mapped back to questions). recipient = where
-- Workflow C last emailed them (already test-mode rewritten) — never users.email — and NULL
-- when that address has since been suppressed. Zero rows = unknown user.
-- $1 user_id
SELECT u.user_id, u.name, u.age, u.employment_status::text AS employment_status, u.monthly_income, u.credit_score,
       u.last_batch_id::text AS batch_id,
       d.answers AS declared, coalesce(d.flagged, false) AS flagged,
       (SELECT l.recipient
          FROM (SELECT n.recipient FROM notifications n
                 WHERE n.user_id = u.user_id AND n.status = 'SENT'
                 ORDER BY n.sent_at DESC NULLS LAST, n.id DESC LIMIT 1) l
         WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM suppression x
                           WHERE x.email_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(lower(l.recipient), 'UTF8')), 'hex'))) AS recipient,
       (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(x ORDER BY x.score DESC, x.product_id), '[]'::json)
          FROM (SELECT m.product_id, m.status, m.score, m.unverified, m.decided_by,
                       p.lender_name, p.product_name, p.source_url, p.interest_rate_min, p.interest_rate_max,
                       p.max_loan_amount, p.min_monthly_income, p.min_credit_score, p.min_age, p.max_age,
                       p.employment_types::text[] AS employment_types,
                       CASE WHEN m.status = 'LIKELY' THEN p.soft_rules ELSE '[]'::jsonb END AS soft_rules
                  FROM matches m JOIN loan_products p ON p.id = m.product_id
                 WHERE m.user_id = u.user_id AND p.is_active) x) AS matches
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN user_declarations d USING (user_id)
WHERE u.user_id = $1;

-- Workflow D: everything the form and the re-check need for ONE person, as one row.
-- matches = all of the person's matches on active products (LIKELY ones carry the product's
-- soft_rules so unverified rule texts can be mapped back to questions). recipient = where
-- Workflow C last emailed them (already test-mode rewritten) — never users.email — and NULL
-- when that address has since been suppressed. Zero rows = unknown user.
-- $1 user_id
SELECT u.user_id, u.name, u.age, u.employment_status::text AS employment_status, u.monthly_income, u.credit_score,
       u.last_batch_id::text AS batch_id,
       d.answers AS declared, coalesce(d.flagged, false) AS flagged,
       (SELECT l.recipient
          FROM (SELECT n.recipient FROM notifications n
                 WHERE n.user_id = u.user_id AND n.status = 'SENT'
                 ORDER BY n.sent_at DESC NULLS LAST, n.id DESC LIMIT 1) l
         WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM suppression x
                           WHERE x.email_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(lower(l.recipient), 'UTF8')), 'hex'))) AS recipient,
       (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(x ORDER BY x.score DESC, x.product_id), '[]'::json)
          FROM (SELECT m.product_id, m.status, m.score, m.unverified, m.decided_by,
                       p.lender_name, p.product_name, p.source_url, p.interest_rate_min, p.interest_rate_max,
                       p.max_loan_amount, p.min_monthly_income, p.min_credit_score, p.min_age, p.max_age,
                       p.employment_types::text[] AS employment_types,
                       CASE WHEN m.status = 'LIKELY' THEN p.soft_rules ELSE '[]'::jsonb END AS soft_rules
                  FROM matches m JOIN loan_products p ON p.id = m.product_id
                 WHERE m.user_id = u.user_id AND p.is_active) x) AS matches
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN user_declarations d USING (user_id)
WHERE u.user_id = $1;

-- Store a person's self-declared answers (merged with any earlier ones by the Code node).
-- Contradictory answers are kept for ops but flagged, and the batch timeline gets a 'confirm'
-- event straight away (nothing else happens for a flagged person). `unlocked` is cumulative and
-- only workflow D's apply step changes it.
-- $1 user_id, $2 batch_id ('' = none), $3 answers JSON, $4 flagged ('true'/'false'), $5 flag_reasons JSON
WITH saved AS (
  INSERT INTO user_declarations AS d (user_id, batch_id, answers, flagged, flag_reasons)
  VALUES ($1, nullif($2, '')::uuid, $3::jsonb, $4::boolean, $5::jsonb)
  ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE
     SET batch_id = coalesce(EXCLUDED.batch_id, d.batch_id), answers = EXCLUDED.answers,
         flagged = EXCLUDED.flagged, flag_reasons = EXCLUDED.flag_reasons, updated_at = now()
  RETURNING d.user_id, d.batch_id, d.flagged
), ev AS (
  INSERT INTO pipeline_events (batch_id, stage, status, detail)
  SELECT batch_id, 'confirm', 'completed', jsonb_build_object('unlocked', 0, 'flagged', true)
  FROM saved WHERE flagged
)
SELECT user_id, batch_id::text AS batch_id, flagged FROM saved;

-- Apply the re-check of ONE person's LIKELY matches in a single set-based statement.
--   unlock → ELIGIBLE, decided_by 'DECLARED', nothing left to confirm
--   narrow → still LIKELY with fewer conditions          reject → match deleted
-- Only rows still LIKELY are touched, so a double submit can't count an unlock twice.
-- Also adds the unlocks to user_declarations.unlocked and logs a 'confirm' event for the batch.
-- $1 user_id, $2 decisions JSON [{product_id, action, score, unverified}]
WITH dec AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($2::jsonb) AS x(product_id bigint, action text, score real, unverified jsonb)
), removed AS (
  DELETE FROM matches m USING dec
  WHERE m.user_id = $1 AND m.product_id = dec.product_id AND dec.action = 'reject' AND m.status = 'LIKELY'
  RETURNING m.product_id
), changed AS (
  UPDATE matches m
     SET status     = CASE WHEN dec.action = 'unlock' THEN 'ELIGIBLE' ELSE 'LIKELY' END,
         decided_by = CASE WHEN dec.action = 'unlock' THEN 'DECLARED' ELSE m.decided_by END,
         unverified = CASE WHEN dec.action = 'unlock' THEN '[]'::jsonb ELSE coalesce(dec.unverified, m.unverified) END,
         score      = dec.score
    FROM dec
   WHERE m.user_id = $1 AND m.product_id = dec.product_id AND dec.action IN ('unlock', 'narrow') AND m.status = 'LIKELY'
  RETURNING m.product_id, m.status
), opened AS (
  SELECT count(*)::int AS n, coalesce(jsonb_agg(product_id ORDER BY product_id), '[]'::jsonb) AS ids
  FROM changed WHERE status = 'ELIGIBLE'
), decl AS (
  UPDATE user_declarations d SET unlocked = d.unlocked + (SELECT n FROM opened), updated_at = now()
  WHERE d.user_id = $1
  RETURNING d.batch_id
), ev AS (
  INSERT INTO pipeline_events (batch_id, stage, status, detail)
  SELECT batch_id, 'confirm', 'completed',
         jsonb_build_object('unlocked', (SELECT n FROM opened), 'flagged', false,
                            'narrowed', (SELECT count(*) FROM changed WHERE status = 'LIKELY'),
                            'removed', (SELECT count(*) FROM removed))
  FROM decl
)
SELECT (SELECT n FROM opened) AS unlocked, (SELECT ids FROM opened) AS unlocked_ids,
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM changed WHERE status = 'LIKELY') AS narrowed,
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM removed) AS removed;

-- After SES accepted the "you now pre-qualify" email: stamp the unlocked matches as notified.
-- $1 user_id, $2 JSON array of product ids
UPDATE matches SET notified_at = now()
WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id IN (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb)::bigint)
RETURNING product_id;
